tagline.text: Learn about organic farming and eat farm-fresh on the slopes of Mt. Banahaw

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Gagalot, Majayjay, Laguna (beside San Isidro Labrador Chapel)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~2,000 (day tour per person, lodging extra)

children.text: An organic model farm on the foothills of Mt. Banahaw in Majayjay, Laguna. Introduced as the first farm tourism site accredited by the Department of Tourism (DOT), it offers vegetable harvesting, salad making and farm stays as a day trip or an overnight visit.

Costales Nature Farm is an organic farm and agri-tourism site in Barangay Gagalot, Majayjay, Laguna. It is sometimes described as being in Magdalena, but its actual address is Majayjay; Magdalena is only a fork in the road that you meet when coming up from the Pagsanjan side. Set at about
above sea level on the foothills of Mt. Banahaw, it feels like a highland retreat with cooler temperatures than the lowlands.

The farm began in 2005, when Ronald and Josephine Costales, a couple from the IT industry, bought the land. They moved to Majayjay the following year and started growing organic vegetables for their own family. As word of mouth brought more visitors, it grew into the farm tourism site it is today. It is also a working production farm that supplies organic vegetables to hotels and restaurants such as Italianni's and Solaire. It is introduced as the first site the Department of Tourism accredited as agri-tourism, and it also runs a TESDA-accredited training center for organic agriculture.

For travelers, this is less a place to look at than a place to do things. A guide takes you past compost and EM (effective microorganism) soil technology, the seedling nursery, the vermiculture greenhouse, free-range chickens and rabbits, and the pig pens. You pick lettuce yourself and make a salad, and pick herbs to brew tea. Lunch is Filipino home cooking made with ingredients picked in the field, which suits families with children and city workers who need a break.
It takes about
2.5–3 hours

one way from Manila, so a day trip is possible, but to enjoy the quiet foothills properly we recommend an overnight farm stay. It also combines well with a highland Laguna–Quezon route that includes the Kamay ni Hesus shrine in nearby Lucban, the slipper street of Liliw and Majayjay Falls. Rates and tour packages change from year to year, so treat the amounts below as a rough guide and confirm with the farm when you book.

With a guide you walk through Farm A and see compost, EM soil technology, urban container gardening, the seedling nursery and the vermiculture greenhouse in turn. You also pass the free-range chickens, rabbits and pig pens. The explanations are easy to follow even if you have never farmed, so children rarely get bored.

The signature activity is making a salad from lettuce and herbs you pick yourself and tossing it in the farm's house vinaigrette. There is also a program where you pay by weight for vegetables you harvest, which is a good way to bring home vegetables for the week.

You pick spearmint, tarragon and blue ternate flowers, steep them, and sweeten the tea with honey and calamansi. You can also make cucumber juice and kale juice yourself, and the tea brewed from the blue flowers has an unusual color.

Many visitors say fishing for tilapia and catfish (hito) in the ponds works best in the morning, and small fish are often returned to the water. Chasing chickens to collect eggs and feeding the animals are also popular with children.

Lunch, made with vegetables from the field and pork and chicken raised on the farm, is the highlight of the tour. Mushroom soup, crispy pork liempo, ginataang kale and longganisa made from organic pork come up often in reviews. The farm is also known to serve pancit habhab as a welcome snack.

You stay in a bahay kubo or in villas built in a traditional Filipino style. Some rooms have a small balcony overlooking the farm and the mountain, and rooms range from huts for two to villas for up to ten. At night you can enjoy the foothills, which are much quieter than the city.

blocks.title: Organic products from the shop and deli

children.text: The farm shop sells potted herbs, seedlings, organic juices and wines, household goods and the house vinaigrette. You can eat at the restaurant Apong Damian's Organic Resto and buy organic food at the deli The Right Food.

For student groups there are pre-tour orientations and lessons in organic agriculture, farm tourism, farm business management and organic culinary arts. Many families, schools and companies visit in groups, and for large groups the rates and schedule can be adjusted.
Arrive at the farm, register and listen to a short orientation. The order of activities can change with your arrival time, so tell the farm your arrival time when you book.
Start the guided farm tour with a guide. You pass the seedling nursery, the vermiculture greenhouse, the compost area and the animal pens in turn.
Morning snack time. Rest with herbal tea and juice.
Join hands-on activities such as sowing seeds, transplanting herbs, harvesting vegetables, and making salad and juice. If you want to fish, head to the ponds around this time.
Eat a farm-to-table lunch made from ingredients picked in the field.
Finish the tour and browse the shop for potted herbs and organic products. One listing says guests should arrive by
at the latest, so do not start out late.

This timetable is the sample schedule of a half-day experience package. The farm will confirm the actual hours and order when you book. Many listings show Monday as a closing day, so check the day you plan to visit.
Arrive at the farm, drop your bags and begin with a welcome snack and herbal tea. Confirm the check-in time when you book.
Take the farm tour and try lettuce picking and salad making.
Have lunch, then rest in your room or stroll around the farm.
If you ask the farm, it can arrange a nearby trip such as Majayjay Falls or Liliw. If you would rather relax, enjoy the mountain view from your balcony.
After dinner, enjoy the quiet farm at night.
On the second day, get up early and try pond fishing. Many reviews say the morning bite is better.
After breakfast, check out and head to the Kamay ni Hesus shrine in Lucban or return to Manila.
Lodging packages are divided by room type for 2 to 10 people. A 3-day, 2-night wellness tour is also listed, but check whether it is currently offered.

Tell the van driver in advance to drop you off at Costales Nature Farm. Vehicles bound for Lucban pass in front of the farm.
You can also take a bus to Santa Cruz, then a jeepney from the market to Majayjay and another jeepney toward Lucban, but the many transfers take longer.

. Allow plenty of time.
From Manila, head toward Calamba and Pagsanjan and then climb the mountain road. Reviews advise taking the Majayjay direction (left) at both forks where the road splits toward Majayjay and Magdalena.
If you enter Costales Nature Farms in your navigation app, it will lead you to the entrance in Barangay Gagalot. The main gate is beside San Isidro Labrador Chapel.
It takes about
2.5–3 hours
from Manila, depending on traffic.
You get around the farm on foot. Dirt paths can be slippery in the rain, so sneakers or trekking shoes are safer than sandals.
The farm is known to arrange trips to nearby waterfalls, Liliw and Lucban if you ask.

Farm activities are mostly outdoors, so the dry season with less rain is the most comfortable. From December to May you can enjoy the fields and ponds freely, and being in the foothills it is cooler than the lowlands.

June to November is the rainy and typhoon season. Rain makes the fields muddy and can make pond fishing and visits to nearby waterfalls difficult, though the farm looks greener. On days with a typhoon warning it is safer to postpone, and you should confirm the cancellation and change policy when you book.

Lodging is in traditional Filipino-style houses on the farm. The rooms listed include the bahay kubo and Balai Liwayway for two, Villa Josefa for three, and Villa Marcus and Villa Angela for up to ten. Rooms have a small balcony with a view of the farm and are simply furnished. Cooling and hot water vary by room, so confirm when you book. If your group is large, ask the farm to tailor group rates and meal plans.

Meals are said to be at the farm restaurant, Apong Damian's Organic Resto, and you can buy organic food and snacks at the deli The Right Food. If your package does not include lunch you need to order meals separately, and outside food is restricted according to one listing. Tell the farm about vegetarian diets or allergies when you book. There is no convenience store near the farm, so it is safer to bring snacks, basic medicine and water.

Before you go, confirm the tour type, rates and open days and make a reservation through the farm's Facebook page or by email (inquiries@costalesnaturefarms.com). Many listings show Monday as a closing day.
Wear sneakers or trekking shoes suited to dirt paths and clothes you do not mind sweating in. A hat, sunscreen and insect repellent are also handy.
If you ride a van, tell the driver before departure to let you off at Costales so you do not pass it.
Some programs sell lettuce and herbs by weight, so bring a cooler bag or a large plastic bag to carry vegetables home.
Fishing is said to be best in the morning, so if you stay overnight, try it on the second morning.
If you travel with children, ask for a program of short activities such as feeding animals, chasing chickens and picking lettuce.
If you want to combine nearby waterfalls, Liliw and Lucban, ask the farm to arrange a tour or arrange a local vehicle through your lodging.
Bring plenty of cash in small bills. Confirm whether card payment is accepted when you book.
The official website address (costalesnaturefarms.com) was found to redirect to another site, so make reservations and payments only through the farm's official Facebook page or by email.
Rates found online mix reviews from 2016 to 2022 and differ from one another. Always ask the farm for the latest rates.
Hours on sites such as Tripadvisor (
, closed Mondays) are third-party information, so confirm before you go.
One review complains about the farm's investment offer. If you receive an investment or lot-sale offer, verify it directly before signing anything.
In the typhoon and rainy season, mountain roads are dangerous and waterfall visits may be canceled, so check the weather forecast.
The farm has free-range animals and ponds, so do not leave children alone. Farm B is for production and is off-limits to visitors.
A town in Quezon province a short drive from the farm, known for the Kamay ni Hesus shrine and local food such as longganisa. The farm sometimes arranges tours there.
A small Laguna town famous for its street of slipper and shoe workshops. It is a nearby route often combined with a farm tour.
A nearby waterfall that is sometimes included in the farm's Green Living tour. Confirm water conditions and how to enter with the farm.
A waterfall on the Luisiana side, listed as one of the places the farm offers as a nearby tour. There is a walking section, so bring sturdy shoes.
